//: Acknowledgements that a counted architecture file changed WITHOUT the census being re-measured. Read by src/scripts/checkCensusFreshness.ts. An entry names the census, the head_commit it was written against (`since`), the FILES it covers, and why those changes cannot have moved a verdict. It covers the paths it names and nothing else — a counted file that changed and is not listed in `files` makes the census stale again, and an entry with no `files` covers nothing. It is spent the moment that census is re-measured: the checker compares `since` against the census head_commit and FAILS on a mismatch, so an acknowledgement cannot outlive the measurement it was written for. A second array, `retired`, holds acknowledgements whose census was later re-declared at a reachable commit: the checker does not read it, and it exists so that the per-file argument that justified the re-declaration survives the entry that carried it.

acknowledged.reason:
ONE counted file changed, and the change was made while re-deriving the very rows that rest on it, so this is a measured delta rather than an unexamined one. buildCrewCard now checks the live-share grant's own expiresAt against the `now` it already receives, and fails closed on an unparseable timestamp. Before, `raw.liveShare != null` was the whole test and the comment at :182 asserted "the GRANT has not expired" as a premise.

WHY NO TRIPS VERDICT MOVES. The four C rows graded against this file were re-read against the code in the same pass: TR10 (no global location tracker), TR110 (canSeePreciseLocation), TR160 (expires_at) and TR179 (no covert persistent tracking). All four were TRUE before this change and are true after. They were true before because TripCrewLocationService — the only caller, verified by reading it — filters `.gt("expires_at", now)` in SQL and gates on allowed_member_ids.includes(viewerId). The change moves those rows from true-because-a-neighbour-filters to true-by-construction. Strictly more restrictive, and only in a state the service already prevented from arriving.

CHECKABLE, not asserted: 7 new tests, 5 of which failed against the unfixed guard, plus 78/78 across tripCrewLocation, tripCrewStatusAndPrivacy and the new file. Both rules mutation-tested. The citations this edit shifted were re-anchored in the same commit — check:doc-citations went from 6 broken anchors to clean, and the anchored floor rose 278 -> 281.

SECOND FILE, added 2026-09-11 when the trips scope was widened 38 -> 104 of the 118 files this census cites: `src/test/tripsCensusRederivation.test.ts` is NEW, created by §38 to pin the 37 C-row invariants that pass re-derived. A new test cannot move a verdict — it adds evidence for rows that already held, and every assertion in it was mutation-tested, including one that initially could NOT fail and was rewritten. It is named here rather than left uncovered because an acknowledgement covers the paths it names and nothing else.

THIRD FILE, 2026-09-11: `src/routes/trips.ts`. WHAT CHANGED: POST /trips now parses CreateTripSchema before using req.body, closing the primary create against census-trips TR51 (which moved C -> W on the measurement that 8 of 53 trip write endpoints read req.body with no schema). Nine tests, five of which failed against the unvalidated endpoint. No Trips verdict moves on this file BECAUSE OF the change: TR51's move was caused by the measurement, not by the edit, and is already recorded in the document and in the restated headline (89 -> 88 C, 127 -> 128 W). The rows graded on this file's authorization gates — TR52, TR106, TR107 — were re-derived in the same pass and hold; the five citations this edit shifted were re-anchored in the same commit and check:doc-citations is clean.

ONE counted file changed: buildCrewCard now enforces the live-share grant's own expiry instead of trusting that a caller filtered it.

WHY NO MAP VERDICT MOVES, and why this census watches the file at all. census-map grades no row against lib/tripCrewLocation.ts. It scopes it because of a METHOD BLIND SPOT this document records at its own header: this census scored only artifacts citing the Map spec, so a file citing Trips was invisible to it, and the stale-crew-location defect had to be found by the Trips census instead (fixed in 0b4f1934). The path is in scope so that blind spot cannot recur — it is a tripwire, not a graded artifact.

The change is in the same family as the defect that put it here (freshness/privacy of crew location) and is strictly more restrictive: it withholds exact coordinates in one state — an expired grant reaching the guard — that the Map never observes, because TripCrewLocationService filters expired sessions in SQL before any card is built. Nothing this census measures about the social_zone layer, marker freshness or people-bearing readers is touched. The tripwire fired, was read, and is answered here rather than silenced.

FOUND BY WIDENING THE SCOPE, which is the point. This census watched 22 of the 72 files it cites (31%) until 2026-09-11; the scope covered services/trust/ — what was being BUILT — and left unwatched the call sites and suites its six W->C rows actually rest on. Widened to 69 of 72 (96%), and the very first run reported this file STALE. Nothing had noticed it before because nothing was looking.

WHY NO TRUST VERDICT MOVES. One row grades this file: C10, `getDisplayTrustScore` is THE display number and there is no second engine. Re-read at HEAD: PassportProjectionService still reads through getDisplayTrustScore (imported at :34, called at :1181), no second scoring path was introduced, and the three added fields are additive metadata about what the existing number rests on — they do not compute a score. C10 holds.

THE CITATION HAD ROTTED, and this is the §37 class showing up in a second census: C10 cited `PassportProjectionService.ts:1015` and the read is now at :1181, off by 166 lines. It stayed IN RANGE, so check:doc-citations was green on it the whole time. FOUR files, one reason each, because this ledger now covers only what it names.

(1) lib/memoryOutbox.ts — the change adds 48 lines and NOT ONE OF THEM IS CODE. Verified mechanically, not from a commit message: `git diff cdfff599..HEAD -- src/lib/memoryOutbox.ts` filtered to lines that are neither comment nor blank returns EMPTY, against a --stat of 48 insertions / 0 deletions. The added text records four facts the outbox-certification lane measured on portava-ci for whoever writes the section-18 worker: nothing acks a row, there is no poison handling, now() is transaction-start time, and the outbox row does not carry `sequence`.

(2) services/memoryProjections/derivativeRegistry.ts and (3) .../derivativeRegistryRead.ts — a SPLIT, not a change of what is built. readRegisteredPayload moved out so the projection has a consumer that is not its own producer (check:projection-consumers found the old shape and was right). Every exported function that existed still exists, with the same signature and the same SQL; the serve path issues its own SELECT with the same columns and filters rather than delegating, because importing back would have made the two modules an ESM cycle. NO section-18 or section-15 requirement changes built/not-built status: nothing was added, nothing was removed, one function changed file.

(4) services/memoryRetrieval/searchMemories.ts — ONE line changed, an import path, from derivativeRegistry.js to derivativeRegistryRead.js. Nothing else in the file moved.

CHECKABLE, not asserted: the three suites that pin this code — memoryProjectionRegistry.test.ts, memoryRetrievalSearch.test.ts and projectionConsumers.test.ts — are 73 pass / 0 fail after the split, and the only edit any of them needed was the same import path. A split that had moved a verdict would have moved an assertion.
retired.retiredBecause: RETIRED 2026-09-10, not withdrawn. Each of these three censuses declared a PRE-SQUASH head_commit — `cdfff599`, `743ae78f`, `9f8122ff` — and this repository squash-merges, so every one of them is an ancestor of nothing, sits on no remote branch, and exists only in the clone that wrote it. Reproduced in a fresh clone on 2026-09-10: `git diff <commit>..HEAD` aborts with `Invalid revision range`, and check:census-freshness reported all three as unreadable rather than checking them (`CENSUS_HEAD_COMMITS_UNREACHABLE_IN_CI`). The three censuses now declare `42aeac38`, which is on `main`. That re-declaration made these entries spent by the checker's own rule — `since` must equal the census's CURRENT head_commit — so leaving them in `acknowledged` would hard-fail the run. They are moved here rather than deleted because the ARGUMENT is the thing worth keeping: the re-declaration is only defensible if these files really did change nothing a verdict rests on, and each argument below was re-verified mechanically on 2026-09-10 at `<original>..42aeac38` before the move. Nothing reads this array; it is a record.
